what_its_for: Tadalafil is used to treat erectile dysfunction (trouble getting or keeping an erection), symptoms of an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH) such as trouble urinating, and a type of high blood pressure in the lungs called pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). It works by relaxing the muscles and increasing blood flow to certain areas of the body.
how_to_take: Take tadalafil by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. If you are taking it as needed for erectile dysfunction, take it at least 30 minutes before sexual activity. If you are taking it once daily, take it at the same time each day. Do not take more than your doctor prescribed.
dosing: For erectile dysfunction as needed: the usual starting dose is 10 mg, which may be adjusted to 5 mg or 20 mg based on how well it works for you. For once-daily erectile dysfunction or BPH: the usual dose is 2.5 mg to 5 mg once a day. For pulmonary arterial hypertension (Adcirca/Alyq): the usual dose is 40 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you take tadalafil once daily and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. If you take tadalafil only as needed before sexual activity, there is no regular schedule to follow, so a missed dose does not apply.
storage: Store tadalafil at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program near you.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink large amounts of alcohol while taking tadalafil, as this can increase your risk of low blood pressure, dizziness, and headache. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they can increase the level of tadalafil in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Do not take tadalafil if you also use nitrate medicines (such as nitroglycerin, isosorbide) for chest pain or heart problems — combining these can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure. Avoid riociguat (Adempas) and recreational drugs called 'poppers' (amyl nitrate or nitrite). Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: an erection that lasts more than 4 hours (priapism) — this is a medical emergency; sudden vision loss in one or both eyes; sudden decrease or loss of hearing, possibly with ringing in the ears or dizziness; chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or shortness of breath during or after sex; severe dizziness or fainting; a serious allergic reaction (rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, trouble breathing). Also contact your doctor if you experience back pain or muscle aches, as this is a common side effect that usually goes away in 1–2 days.
when_it_works: If taken as needed for erectile dysfunction, tadalafil usually starts working within 30 minutes to 1 hour and can remain effective for up to 36 hours — that is why it is sometimes called 'the weekend pill.' If taken once daily, it keeps a steady level in your body so you can be ready at any time. For BPH symptoms, you may notice improvement within a few weeks of daily use. For pulmonary arterial hypertension, it may take several weeks to feel the full benefit.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): No automatic dose adjustment is needed, but older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like low blood pressure and dizziness, so start with caution. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may prescribe a lower dose or ask you to take it less often if your kidneys or liver are not working well. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tadalafil (Adcirca/Alyq for PAH) may be used in pregnancy only if clearly needed; talk to your doctor about the risks. It is not known if tadalafil passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Safety and effectiveness have not been established in children for erectile dysfunction or BPH. For PAH in children, use is determined by a specialist.
